newsitem.title: CANADA: ALPINE SKIING-MEN'S DOWNHILL TRAINING SCRUBBED.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-MEN'S DOWNHILL TRAINING SCRUBBED.

text.p: Heavy fog and soft snow forced cancellation of training on Thursday for Saturday's first World Cup men's downhill race of the season.
Two training runs have been scheduled for Friday in preparation for the race. At least one training run is required before the downhill.
"There's a lot of (soft) snow on the course, but the major concern was the fog," Canadian veteran Brian Stemmle said. "If it gets a little colder, the course will be hard and fast."
The World Cup downhill season begins in Canada after several years of cancellations at Val d'Isere in the French Alps due to poor snow conditions.
There is a lot of snow at Whistler, but conditions have not cooperated. A heavy snow Wednesday cancelled the first scheduled training run.
A super-giant slalom is scheduled for Sunday.
